ac_verbatim: Each target has a pinned engine/toolchain, dictionary/corpus digest, minimum bounded campaign, timeout/OOM/crash policy, artifact capture, replay command, and exact target manifest; unavailable tooling blocks instead of skipping.
note: This manifest is the AC3 exact target manifest AND the honest AC2 census. It is CHECKED, not asserted: cmd/fuzzpinctl -check re-derives every digest from the tree, requires each declared entrypoint to be a real #[test] fn in the named file, and requires each declared campaign size and generator seed to appear VERBATIM as the loop literal in that source. The defect class it exists to stop is existence standing in for identity -- a seed corpus on disk is not a campaign, a property test is not a fuzz target, and a replay command nobody ran is a string. All seven AC2 families now carry a dedicated generative target and are recorded PINNED: three were ABSENT (handshake-client, handshake-server, owner-driver-command-byte-schedules) and two were SHARED_NO_DEDICATED_TARGET (fragment-control-sequences, close-eof). What those earlier entries said about the OLD tree remains true of the files they named -- adversarial_fuzz.rs still gives the handshake parsers no coverage, still draws its frames independently of one another, and still emits EOF in exactly one family -- and each sentence is preserved inside the new rationale that replaced it, so the record cannot be read as if the gap never existed. The coverage-guided engine (cargo-fuzz/libFuzzer) is still not installed in this environment and is still recorded UNAVAILABLE, which BLOCKS: it is not skipped and it is not claimed. Every campaign here is DETERMINISTIC and BOUNDED -- fixed committed seeds, no coverage feedback, no corpus evolution. Bounded evidence, never proof.

targets.rationale: A real generative target as of rust/ws-core/tests/handshake_fuzz.rs: response bytes are GENERATED and driven through ClientHandshake. Two generation modes. (1) Modeled: draw_response_model draws a HeadModel -- version/status/reason first-line tokens from alphabets that include TAB-padded variants, a drawn header multiset with duplicate, case-varied, space- and TAB-padded, and folded forms, a drawn Sec-WebSocket-Accept that is sometimes the correctly derived value and sometimes a near-miss, and drawn line terminators -- renders it to bytes, and predicts the verdict from the MODEL without re-parsing the rendering, so the differential is model-vs-implementation and not implementation-vs-itself. One case in four is corrupted after rendering, and half of the modeled cases are NEAR-VALID (the canonical head with exactly one element perturbed) because a uniform generator dies at the first line and never reaches the deeper clauses. (2) Seed-derived: the 11 committed us010 seeds are read as generator INPUT and mutated (byte flips, truncations, splices, header injection), instead of being replayed at the fixed expectations of handshake_seeds.rs. Oracles: no panic under catch_unwind, terminal stickiness, determinism, rechunking invariance over a chunk-invariant projection that recovers head_len as an absolute offset, the model differential, and bounded buffering under drawn small budgets. Claim grade: bounded. This is a DETERMINISTIC BOUNDED campaign at fixed committed seeds -- no coverage feedback, no corpus evolution, and no crash minimizer beyond the in-file shrinker.

corpus.note: handshake_client_seed_mutations reads every file under this tree through committed_seeds("us010") and asserts the count is still 11, so a silent corpus deletion fails the target as well as this digest.

liveness_guard.note: F005: the guard against non-termination is a wall-clock deadline, never a count. The 16,300 deterministic cases are WORK (they fix what is explored so outcomes reproduce); they are not the liveness bound. The whole handshake_fuzz binary -- both families plus the shrinker pins -- was observed at 4.9s on an unloaded run of this host; 900s leaves roughly 180x headroom so concurrent agents cannot turn slowness into a spurious failure.

policy.crash: Every parser drive runs inside catch_unwind (drive_client / judge_client); a panic FAILS the case with its labelled seed and case index, the test binary exits nonzero, and the campaign fails. Panics are never swallowed.
policy.timeout: cmd/fuzzpinctl kills the replay process at the declared wall-clock deadline via context.WithTimeout and records deadline_hit=true, which FAILS the campaign. A killed run is never reported as a pass.
policy.oom: The bounded-buffering oracle asserts that a parse refused over budget never retained more than the drawn max_handshake_bytes plus the pinned wire slack, and the shrinker asserts a strictly decreasing byte length so a runaway shrink cannot allocate without bound. An OOM kill produces a nonzero ProcessState exit and fails through the same path as any other nonzero exit; the runner reads the exit code from the real process state and never invents one.

targets.rationale: The same generator shaped for the other parser: rust/ws-core/tests/handshake_fuzz.rs GENERATES request bytes and drives ServerHandshake over them. draw_request_model draws method/target/version first-line tokens (including TAB-padded variants, which is the padding that separates a literal comparison from a trimmed one), a drawn header multiset with duplicate, case-varied, padded and folded forms, a drawn Sec-WebSocket-Key that is sometimes a valid 16-byte base64 and sometimes a near-miss, and drawn terminators; the verdict is predicted from the MODEL, not from re-parsing the rendering. handshake_server_seed_mutations turns the 17 committed us011 seeds into generator INPUT. This replaces the census entry that read: family_seed_corpus_anchors in adversarial_fuzz.rs DOES read the us010/us011 hex files, but it feeds them to ConnectionCore as post-handshake FRAME bytes, so the handshake parsers got no coverage from it at all -- that remains true of adversarial_fuzz.rs, and is why this separate target exists. Oracles are the client target's, over the server verdict. Claim grade: bounded; deterministic and fixed-seed, not coverage-guided.

targets.rationale: A real generative target: rust/ws-core/tests/adversarial_fuzz.rs draws random transport chunks and structured adversarial frames from a hand-rolled SplitMix64 PRNG at fixed committed seeds, independently of the shipped encoder, and drives ConnectionCore under catch_unwind with no-panic, bounded-allocation, determinism, and rechunk-invariance oracles. This is a DETERMINISTIC BOUNDED generative campaign, NOT coverage-guided fuzzing: it has no coverage feedback, no corpus evolution, and no crash-artifact minimizer. Claim grade: bounded. total_cases counts only entrypoints with a fixed generated-case loop; family_seed_corpus_anchors (corpus replay across 3 setups x 3 chunkings) and family_declared_length_headers (9 curated declarations x 2 roles) carry cases:0 because they generate no case loop, and their drives are therefore NOT in the 29,000.

targets.rationale: A dedicated generative target as of rust/ws-core/tests/fragment_control_fuzz.rs, with its own campaign bound, its own artifact directory, and its own replay command. What it generates that the shared coverage could not: the SEQUENCE, not the frame. The census entry this replaces said that draw_frame in adversarial_fuzz.rs draws every opcode and clears FIN one time in five and that draw_stream concatenates one to ten such frames -- all still true, and the point is that those frames are drawn INDEPENDENTLY, so a fragment sequence appears there only by accident and the oracles applied to it (no-panic, bounds, determinism, rechunk) cannot observe whether reassembly produced the RIGHT message, because none of them knows what the right message was. Here the fragments are drawn TOGETHER from one payload and predicted by a MODEL of the documented Java-faithful sites, so reassembly has a right answer that is checked. Families: modeled programs against the model (8,000); control-interleave transparency, where the same fragmentation is re-run with the control frames MOVED (4,000); split-and-rechunk invariance over one payload, two fragmentations and three chunkings (3,000); hostile soup outside the modeled domain with the model dropped (6,000); and a program-level shrinker whose 1-minimality is checked rather than claimed (200 draws) with four byte-pinned normal forms. The target also records a finding about the observable contract: handle_bytes runs a chunk in two stages, so a TRANSLATE-stage rejection anywhere in a chunk means the chunk emits nothing at all, while a PROCESS-stage rejection leaves the earlier frames' events queued. Claim grade: bounded; deterministic and fixed-seed, not coverage-guided.

corpus.note: DECLARED EMPTY ON PURPOSE. This target is seed-free: its whole input is the pinned SplitMix64 seed literals above, and it opens no file. rust/ws-core/fuzz-seeds/us014 and us015 exist and remain pinned -- by the frame-decode target, whose corpus is the WHOLE rust/ws-core/fuzz-seeds tree and whose family_seed_corpus_anchors really does read every *.hex file in it. Repeating a digest here over files this campaign never opens would be existence standing in for identity, which is the defect this manifest exists to stop.

The binary was observed at 6.2s on a loaded run of this host; 900s is deliberately generous so concurrent agents cannot turn slowness into a spurious failure. targets.rationale: A dedicated generative target as of rust/ws-core/tests/close_eof_fuzz.rs, with its own campaign bound, its own artifact directory, and its own replay command. The census entry this replaces named the hole precisely -- EOF was generated only inside family_command_interleave, one step in ten, and byte_soup and frame_soup never emitted EOF at all -- and both halves remain true of adversarial_fuzz.rs. What this target adds is not volume but a different question: the shared coverage asks whether the core survived, while the close/EOF contract is about WHICH close outcome governs. Families: modeled close/EOF schedules compared event-by-event and write-by-write against a model of Q10/Q11/Q12/Q13/Q14/Q19/Q20, including the exact unmasked outbound bytes of the echo and of send_close (7,000); the close-payload parse in isolation at a fixed state, so a parse rejection cannot hide behind a state rejection (6,000); exactly-once terminal plus post-terminal inertness, where a terminated core is hammered with a drawn tail of further EOFs, bytes and commands and must produce no new event of ANY kind, no new write, no change of state or governing detail, and a typed StateViolation for every input (5,000); and hostile soup over both roles with the model dropped (5,000). Claim grade: bounded; deterministic and fixed-seed, not coverage-guided.

targets.rationale: A real generative target at the seam AC2 names: rust/ws-driver/tests/driver_schedule_fuzz.rs DRAWS command/byte/EOF/write-progress/shutdown schedules and runs them against a real ConnectionDriver through the owner poll loop and the transport write path. What it draws: inbound frame bytes built independently of the shipped encoder, all six LocalCommand kinds from two producers over the bounded CommandSender, transport write progress including deliberate overruns, transport EOF, shutdown, and both AutoResponsePolicy and both CloseEchoPolicy values. This is the gap the census recorded: rust/ws-driver/tests/schedule_exploration.rs EXHAUSTIVELY ENUMERATES five fixed actor programs and draws nothing, and family_command_interleave in adversarial_fuzz.rs does draw but against ConnectionCore with no ConnectionDriver, no owner poll loop and no transport write path -- both remain true and neither is this target. Oracles: no panic, determinism, producer purity, write-suffix continuity (a re-offered suffix must be exactly the undrained tail), typed refusal of invalid write progress, exactly-once terminal, US-017 AC2 shutdown accounting against a boundary that independently tracks what the transport still owed, and a bounded-output drain. Coverage floors are asserted at the end of the campaign so generator degeneration cannot pass silently. Claim grade: bounded; deterministic and fixed-seed, not coverage-guided.

corpus.note: DECLARED EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and the honest reading is that this target has no seed corpus. rust/ws-driver/fuzz-seeds/us017 exists (16 files) but this target does not read a byte of it: those files are the US-017 minimizer's byte-for-byte EXPECTED OUTPUT, consumed by the minimizer tests, not seeds fed to a generator. Declaring them here would be a corpus digest over files the campaign never opens -- exactly the existence-standing-in-for-identity defect this manifest exists to stop. The generator's whole input is the pinned SplitMix64 seed literals above, which is why the source_files digest on the splitmix64-in-repo-v1 engine now covers this file.

claim.honest_state: AC2 MET in the sense AC2 states -- every named target family has a generative fuzz target of its own, with its own campaign bound, artifact directory and replay command -- but the manifest may not CLAIM it while a BLOCK stands, and one does, so ac2_met stays false and this sentence is the record instead. AC3 NOT MET: the coverage-guided engine class AC3's vocabulary presumes (pinned engine, dictionary, crash-artifact capture, replay of a MINIMIZED crashing input produced by the engine) is not installed here, so it BLOCKS rather than skipping, and installing it was out of scope. What changed: handshake-client and handshake-server are driven by rust/ws-core/tests/handshake_fuzz.rs, owner-driver-command-byte-schedules by rust/ws-driver/tests/driver_schedule_fuzz.rs, fragment-control-sequences by rust/ws-core/tests/fragment_control_fuzz.rs, and close-eof by rust/ws-core/tests/close_eof_fuzz.rs; frame-decode and message-utf8 are unchanged. What has NOT changed: everything executed here is the in-repo deterministic generative campaign, which is bounded evidence over a fixed, committed, reproducible slice of each input space -- never proof, and never a claim about the inputs it did not draw. Two documented shrinkers exist (handshake_fuzz.rs byte-level, fragment_control_fuzz.rs program-level), each with its generator domain, preserved property, reduction, bound and pinned normal forms stated in source.
